analyst_view.overall: Early view: Lens (11th) sacked Yannick Cahuzac on 9 November, the day after a 2-1 home loss to Marseille and days after a 9-1 Champions League defeat to Como; reports said Pierre Sage was the first choice and Didier Digard the alternative, so a new coach is likely to be on the bench here, with Leipzig three days later. Toulouse (12th, level on 13 points) beat Strasbourg 3-1 last time out under Jens Berthel Askou.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I have moved from level to lower: a new coach with one week of work usually starts by tightening the defence after a 9-1, and one injury list has Lens without both Odsonne Edouard and Abdallah Sima up front. Toulouse score and concede roughly 1.5 a game, so two or three goals looks the likeliest range.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean higher: Lens are 2nd in the league for corners won (5.8 a game) and Toulouse took seven against Strasbourg. Toulouse carry a set-piece threat too, with Mark McKenzie heading in a Cristian Casseres corner last time out.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean slightly higher: Toulouse commit the second-most fouls in Ligue 1 (15.8 a game) and picked up three yellows against Strasbourg, and Lens are 7th for fouls. A Lens side keen to impress a new coach should add intensity, so four or five bookings feels more likely than three.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.0 shots. Season averages agree (Lens 12.9, Toulouse 12.6 a game), so I stay put. A new-coach lift could push Lens' count up, but rotation before Leipzig and missing strikers could pull it down, and those roughly cancel.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I have moved from higher to level: Lens are 4th for shots on target (5.4 a game) and Toulouse average 4.7, but with Edouard and Sima listed as injured Lens' finishing is weaker than their season numbers. Around nine looks right.
